title: Cross-provider REFER transfer continuity and accessibility readiness
objective: Turn ACE Direct transfer behavior into a provider-neutral interoperability scenario that binds the original dialog, REFER transaction, NOTIFY outcome, replacement dialog, referred target identity, and post-transfer accessibility readiness without treating signaling success as a usable handoff.

historicalBasis.observation: ACE Direct routes transfer requests through JsSIP RTCSession.refer(), records REFER subscribers by transaction identity, distinguishes blind versus warm transfer state at the application layer, and hands multiparty host responsibility to a backup agent before the old host terminates its leg.
historicalBasis.scope: Motivating interoperability evidence only. Provider A/B/C identities are synthetic placeholders. Baudot does not infer any behavior of a contemporary VRS provider from the ACE donor or from deterministic or loopback evidence.

providerModel.directions: all ordered pairs where source != target
providerModel.rule: provider identity is configuration, never implementation semantics

assertions: REFER acceptance does not imply a replacement dialog was established
successful NOTIFY status does not imply the replacement leg is accessibility-ready
the replacement dialog must bind to the intended referred target identity
a continuity-preserving transfer must not terminate the old leg before the configured replacement-leg readiness point
provider labels do not alter readiness semantics

proves: all directed provider pairs are represented independently of provider implementation
blind and warm transfer modes remain separate matrix dimensions
REFER acceptance, NOTIFY outcome, replacement-dialog establishment, target correlation, old-leg teardown, and RTT readiness reduce as separate facts
signaling-only transfer success cannot produce an accessibility-ready verdict
premature old-leg teardown is distinguishable from signaling and accessibility failure
replacement-target drift is distinguishable from signaling success
doesNotProve: live SIP REFER or NOTIFY exchange

proves: a live original dialog is established with synthetic provider-a
an in-dialog REFER with a declared provider-b Refer-To target receives 202
progress and terminal Event: refer NOTIFY requests carry message/sipfrag transfer status
the replacement INVITE reaches the independently addressed provider-b target
the replacement dialog reaches 2xx and ACK before final transfer completion
the declared referred target remains correlated to the replacement target
the old leg is torn down only after replacement-dialog establishment and final NOTIFY acknowledgement
doesNotProve: live interoperability with an external provider

proves: the replacement dialog negotiates text/t140 independently of REFER acceptance
a control provider-b sends the repository canonical primary T.140 RTP packet only after replacement ACK
the control old leg is released only after the canonical replacement-leg RTT bytes are observed
the preserved control packet is independently parsed by the Python RFC 4103 reference before firstT140CharacterObserved and rttReady become true
a live signaling-only arm can complete REFER, NOTIFY, replacement 2xx, and ACK while withholding RTT
the signaling-only arm remains rttReady=false and preserves the old leg
doesNotProve: live interoperability with an external provider

runnableEvidence: provider-neutral matrix covering six directed provider pairs and blind/warm dimensions
live JAIN SIP in-dialog REFER with Event: refer NOTIFY progression and replacement-dialog target correlation
independently parsed control T.140 packet producing rttReady=true before old-leg release
live signaling-only transfer producing rttReady=false while the old leg remains preserved
terminal reduction joining signaling, target identity, continuity, and accessibility readiness without collapsing them
requiredBeforeProven: repeatable execution across more than one SIP implementation
all configured provider directions exercised live without provider-specific changes to the reducer
blind and warm transfer coverage with standards-grounded handling of any Replaces usage
failure evidence from additional live implementations for rejected REFER, failed NOTIFY outcome, target mismatch, premature teardown, and accessibility-readiness loss
production-representative gateway or VRS observations without weakening claim boundaries
terminal evidence bundle suitable for an explicit proven-state review

doesNotEstablish: that any named or unnamed provider supports REFER
that ACE Direct transfer behavior is defective or normative
